intro.heading: You have prepared the building and the paperwork. Have you prepared the people?
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: A registered manager has spent weeks on cqc inspection preparation. Audits are done and the actions are closed. Policies have been reviewed and the folders are tidy. At handover she tells everyone that someone may stop them and ask how they keep people safe. The team nods. Nobody has said an answer out loud, and she has never heard the new cook or the night carer explain their own job. The files are ready. What the people will say is a guess. Here is how that plays out.

trail.text: Audits are completed and their actions are closed.
Policies are reviewed, signed off and filed.
The manager reminds everyone that they may be asked questions.
Nobody has practised an answer. Nobody has been asked one.
Knows the allergen sheet. Has never explained it to anyone.
Does the right thing every shift, but may struggle to put it into words.
Strong files. No idea how the team would sound.
“Tell me what you would do if you were worried about a colleague.”

trail_close: The paperwork was never the whole picture. The gap is between what the service has written and what each person can say. Here is how CareStream helps you find that gap in good time.

why.heading: Documents show what you have written. Staff answers show what people know.
why.sub: Good records matter, and so does the person in front of you who has to explain them.

cards.title: Knowing and saying are different skills
cards.body: Many carers do the right thing without thinking. Explaining it to a stranger, calmly and in order, is something people get better at with practice.

cards.title: A reminder at handover is not practice
cards.body: Telling people to be ready does not show you who can answer. It only works if somebody tries, gets feedback and tries again.

cards.title: You cannot sit down with every person
cards.body: Quizzing a whole team yourself takes hours you do not have, and kitchen, domestic and night staff are the people you see least.

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: What does CareStream actually do to get my staff ready?
items.a: It sends each person practice questions in the Staff Hub, grouped by job role, plus a core set for everyone. They answer in their own words and get a score and feedback. You see the results in your analytics. It sits alongside your audits, policy checks and evidence, which cover the paperwork side.

items.q: Will it tell me what an inspector is going to ask?
items.a: No. Nobody can know that in advance, and CareStream does not claim to. The questions are practice questions on the topics that come up in everyday care, such as safeguarding and raising concerns. The point is to help people explain their own work calmly, whatever the actual question turns out to be.

items.q: Is this a rehearsal of the inspection itself?
items.a: No. There is no inspector character and no simulated visit. It is practice for staff, with a score and feedback on each answer. Think of it as a way to hear how your team sounds before it matters.

items.q: How does it work for a cook or a cleaner?
items.a: Staff are grouped by job role, so people are asked about their own work, such as allergens in the kitchen or cleaning schedules for domestic staff. Everyone also gets the core questions on safeguarding, whistleblowing and fire. You choose who takes part.

items.q: What happens when someone gives a weak answer?
items.a: They get feedback on what was missing and can open the model answer, then try again in their own words. Their score can rise on the second go, and you can see the average gain across the team. A weak first answer is useful information, not a mark against anyone.

items.q: What do I see as the manager?
items.a: The average score, the share of answers scoring 80 or more, and how much scores improve after a retry. That tells you whether the team is confident or whether a topic needs a short team talk. Your audits, policy gaps and readiness score sit in the same place.

items.q: Can I show this to an inspector as proof we are ready?
items.a: It is not proof of anything, and nothing in CareStream predicts or proves a CQC rating. What it gives you is your own record of preparation: staff practised, weak answers were revisited and the paperwork was checked. The CQC Inspection Evidence Report, on Professional and above, adds evidence of staff using your policies.

items.q: How do I try it, and what does it cost?
items.a: You can start with a 14 day free trial on the paid plans, or create a free account, which lets you screen up to five policies. Prices are on the pricing page. You can create a free account and be set up in a day.

limits.heading: Practice for your team, not a prediction of the day

cards.title: It does not predict or simulate an inspection
cards.body: There is no inspector persona and no forecast of what will be asked. The questions are practice on everyday topics, and the readiness score is our own blend, not a CQC rating.

cards.title: Scores are practice scores
cards.body: Each answer is marked by our own technology, giving a score and feedback. It is a prompt for a conversation. It does not replace you listening to people, or watching them work.

cards.title: The evidence report is not a pass
cards.body: The CQC Inspection Evidence Report is on Professional and above. It shows staff using your policies over a period you choose. You print it or save it as a PDF from your browser, and it does not combine everything into one download.

items.q: Which CQC inspection questions for staff should we practise?
items.a: There is no fixed list to learn, so practise topics rather than scripts. Start with each person's own job, then the topics everyone shares: safeguarding, whistleblowing, fire and how to raise a concern. CareStream drafts questions for each role plus a core set, and you can see how people get on.

items.q: How does CQC Staff Prep work?
items.a: You choose the staff and they are grouped by job role. Our own machine learning drafts open ended questions for each role plus a core set. Each person gets one email or push notification, answers in the Staff Hub and gets a score and feedback. They can review the model answer and try again. See CQC Staff Prep.

items.q: Do staff need to be in a particular place to answer?
items.a: No. They answer in the Staff Hub, an installable app that works on their own phone, whenever suits them. You choose when to send a round of questions.
No. It sends practice questions to your staff and shows you how they did. There is no inspector character and no prediction of the outcome.

items.q: What does CQC inspection preparation involve beyond staff questions?
items.a: It covers how well your service checks itself and how well people can explain what they do. Regulation 17 on good governance asks for systems and processes that are established and operated effectively, so audits, action tracking and policy checks all belong here. CareStream supports those, alongside staff practice.

items.q: How do I know we are inspection ready?
items.a: Nothing can tell you for certain. CareStream gives you a readiness score that blends your audit results with how well your policies cover the regulations, shown against the five key questions. It is our own score and not a CQC rating, but it shows you where to look first.

items.q: What can I check on the Free plan?
items.a: Audits are free on every plan. On the Free plan you can also screen up to five uploaded policies in total, using all four analyses: regulation coverage, out of date content, consistency between policies and CQC wording. Gap fixes and adopting suggestions are on Professional and above.

items.q: What do the regulations say about staff training and support?
items.a: Regulation 18 on staffing says staff must receive appropriate support, training, professional development, supervision and appraisal. It does not list courses, so each service decides what its people need. Practice questions and follow up training help you see whether it landed.

guide.heading: A practical way to get the team ready for questions
guide.lede: Preparing for an inspection is partly paperwork and partly people. A short, steady routine works better than a rush the week before, and it helps your service be inspection ready all year.

sections.h3: What practice can and cannot do
paragraphs: Practice helps people find the words for work they already do well. It builds confidence, shows who is unsure and gives you something specific to talk through in supervision. It cannot tell you what will be asked, and it does not replace the audits, the policies and the daily care that make up the real picture.
Keep it kind. Staff who feel tested will freeze. Tell the team it is practice, that a weak first answer is useful, and that you will talk through anything that comes up together.

sections.h3: Four steps for the weeks before
checklist: Run your audits and close the actions, with a photo where it helps, then check them again at the next audit.
Check your policies for gaps and out of date wording, and decide which suggested fixes to adopt.
Send each role its own practice questions, plus the core set, and ask people to retry after reading the model answer.
Look at the average scores and the topics that scored lowest, then hold a short team talk on those.

guide.note: For the manager. Keep your results, your actions and your policy checks together, so you can show how you prepared and what you did about the gaps you found.
